description: The Ox in the Chinese zodiac: patience, diligence and steady strength, its Earth element, years from 1961 to 2021, and its San He, Liu He and Liu Chong matches.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Ox is the second animal of the twelve-year cycle, with Earth as its fixed element and Yin polarity. It is traditionally associated with patience, diligence and steady strength. Your animal follows the Lunar New Year of your birth, so early-year birthdays can belong to the previous animal.

sections.heading: The Ox in Chinese astrology
paragraphs: The Ox is the second animal of the cycle and is usually described as patient, dependable and hardworking. In the race story it carried the Rat across the river and finished just behind it, which suits its reputation for steady, generous effort. People born in Ox years are often portrayed as calm, methodical and honest, more interested in doing the work well than in being noticed for it. The Ox's fixed element is Earth and its branch is Chou, linked in the traditional calendar with the cold heart of winter before spring returns. Strength, endurance and loyalty are the recurring keywords. The same steadiness can show up as stubbornness, and descriptions often mention that an Ox takes time to change its mind once it is made up.

Many readers recognise the Ox in a preference for doing things properly the first time, and in a calm that steadies others during a crisis. As a Yin animal, the Ox tends to build quietly rather than announce its plans.

sections.heading: The Ox at work
paragraphs: At work, the Ox is often described as reliable, thorough and willing to take on long, demanding projects. Fields such as engineering, agriculture, medicine, finance, craft, law and administration are commonly mentioned, along with any role where persistence and careful work produce visible results. An Ox tends to earn trust through consistency rather than charm, and colleagues often lean on them in a crisis. The traditional caution is inflexibility: an Ox may resist new methods or keep working in an outdated way because it has always worked before. Readings often suggest that people born in Ox years benefit from building occasional reviews into their routines, and from letting others see the effort behind their quiet competence so that it is properly recognised.

An Ox often performs best with a clear brief and enough time, and it tends to resent being rushed into decisions it has not had space to consider. Managers who give it ownership of long-term work usually find it exceptionally dependable.

sections.heading: The Ox in relationships
paragraphs: In relationships, the Ox is usually described as devoted, protective and slow to commit but steadfast once it does. An Ox shows care through practical support and dependable presence rather than through words. Its classical allies are its San He partners, the Snake and the Rooster, and its Liu He secret friend, the Rat, while the Goat sits opposite it in the six clashes. The common relationship friction is emotional reserve: an Ox may keep feelings private and expect actions to speak for themselves. Partners who are patient, sincere and appreciative of the Ox's steadiness tend to find a deeply loyal companion, especially when they gently invite it to talk rather than waiting for it to volunteer.

Friendships with an Ox tend to be few and lasting. It often shows loyalty by turning up year after year, helping with practical problems and keeping confidences, and it may only reveal its softer side to people it has known for a long time.

sections.heading: Years of the Ox and their elements
paragraphs: Recent and upcoming years of the Ox are 1961 (Metal), 1973 (Water), 1985 (Wood), 1997 (Fire), 2009 (Earth) and 2021 (Metal). Each begins at Lunar New Year rather than on January 1, so people born in January or early February need to check the date: in 1961, for example, the Ox year began on February 15, and anyone born before that is a Metal Rat. The element attached to each year comes from the ten-year cycle of heavenly stems, so a Metal Ox and a Water Ox share the animal's core character but differ in flavour. Separately, the Ox always carries Earth as its fixed element and a Yin polarity, which describe the animal itself. Because the five stem elements and twelve animals line up again only every sixty years, the Wood Ox of 1985 returns in 2045. The Chinese zodiac calculator on this site applies the Lunar New Year table from 1924 to 2044 automatically.

sections.heading: Growth edges for the Ox
paragraphs: The growth edge for the Ox usually involves flexibility and expression. Traditional descriptions mention stubbornness, a tendency to overwork and difficulty letting go of grudges or old routines. An Ox may also find it hard to ask for help, since self-reliance is part of its identity. Practices that tend to help include trying one new approach at a time in low-stakes areas, setting a limit on working hours, and putting appreciation and worry into words. The Ox's gift is endurance and integrity, the ability to keep going and to keep promises. It tends to grow when that strength includes adaptability, so that steadiness becomes a choice that serves the Ox rather than a habit that holds it in place.

In a Unified Reading, the Ox often adds a note of endurance to the wider profile, steadying a restless Life Path or Sun sign, or doubling the patience of a steadier one. For anyone born in an Ox year, these growth notes are prompts for reflection rather than fixed traits.

faq.question: What is the Ox known for in Chinese astrology?
faq.answer: Patience, diligence, reliability and quiet strength. The Ox is often described as the steady worker of the zodiac, honest and loyal, and sometimes stubborn once its mind is made up.

faq.question: Which animals are traditionally best for the Ox?
faq.answer: The Snake and the Rooster share the Ox's San He trine, and the Rat is its Liu He secret friend. The Goat is its Liu Chong clash and the Horse its Liu Hai harm, which traditional readings treat as pairings needing more care.

faq.question: What years are the Year of the Ox?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044 the Ox years are 1925, 1937, 1949, 1961, 1973, 1985, 1997, 2009, 2021 and 2033. Each starts at Lunar New Year, which falls between January 21 and February 20.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Ox?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Snake and Rooster share the Ox's San He trine and the Rat is its Liu He secret friend. The Goat (Liu Chong) and the Horse (Liu Hai) are the pairings readings treat as needing more care.
